commit.message:
Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#34909: wallet, refactor: modularise wallet by extracting out legacy wallet migration

9fd8e543b3ceed08a4bb8ce3d8d342195403056e wallet, refactor: rename file from migrate to legacybdb (rkrux)
f726ef740fae2e73f112a48981fd08cda0ae9c09 wallet: extract out migration specific LegacySPKM CWallet methods (rkrux)
e8165d533191e42ab4f8dd52e9233e13ff8f1262 wallet: extract out public facing MigrateLegacyToDescriptor functions (rkrux)
156249d75e0f9342015dc114fe1cf2210325d094 wallet: extract out utility functions from wallet/wallet to wallet/walletutil.h (rkrux)
5c8b0872b62a35d33461bb6d4c9b306a562b1f63 wallet: (move-only) extract out migration specific CWallet methods (rkrux)

Pull request description:

  I've been meaning to scratch this itch for quite some time. It has been noted
  by many developers that the `wallet/wallet.cpp` file is quite hard to reason
  about.

  It is more than 4500 lines long currently and this patch is an attempt to
  shortern it by around 800 lines by extracting out the wallet migration code into
  a dedicated `wallet/migration.cpp` file.

  The other benefits of this PR I see are that it moves the legacy wallet stuff
  from the main wallet file that paves the way for it being descriptor specific
  (as much as possible), and makes legacy wallet migration code a first-class
  citizen in its own file.

  I hope it makes it easier for everyone to go through the main wallet file.

  This patchset **should** be reviewed with --color-moved=dimmed-zebra option.

commit.message:
Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36908: mining: avoid checkBlock crash when chain has no tip

8cba4bace8df92afcc9ff46404e36c741d557b64 mining: avoid checkBlock crash when chain has no tip (Turtlecute33)

Pull request description:

  **The problem**: `Init.makeMining` returns as soon as the chainstate is loaded. On a first start with an empty datadir, or on a node started with `-reindex`/`-reindex-chainstate`, this is before the genesis block is connected, so the active chain has no tip. A `Mining.checkBlock` call in this window reaches `TestBlockValidity()`, which asserts that the tip exists, and the node aborts.

  **The fix**: in `MakeMining`, if `wait_loaded` is set, wait for the chainstate to be present and for the tip to be non-null.

  *Alternative fix*: In `Mining.checkBlock`, check if the tip is present, return early with "inconclusive-no-chain-tip" otherwise. (I initially implemented this fix, but decided to go with the `makeMining` one instead, see https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36908#discussion_r4610682758)

  The crash can be reproduced on master using the functional test included in this PR.

  This is joint work with Turtlecute33 :)

    ACK 8cba4bace8df92afcc9ff46404e36c741d557b64
  w0xlt:
    ACK 8cba4bace8df92afcc9ff46404e36c741d557b64
  xyzconstant:
    tACK 8cba4bace8
  ryanofsky:
    Code review ACK 8cba4bace8df92afcc9ff46404e36c741d557b64. This extends the #34661 fix to cover a case it missed. #34661 made `makeMining` wait for the chainstate to be loaded, but on a first start or with `-reindex`/`-reindex-chainstate` the chainstate is loaded before genesis is connected, and a `checkBlock` call in between still hits the `Tip()` assert in `TestBlockValidity`. `makeMining` now also waits for a tip using the same condition `AppInitMain` waits for before starting the node.

commit.message:
Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36863: test: fix wallet tests that check the wrong wallet

13b2d21bebb0d84847e1c42f96db280058e7b0a6 test: check w8, not w7, after creating the avoid_reuse wallet (w0xlt)
215f8b828bc5c85b6a662c1424902e25c23ec6c0 test: restore each node's own wallet backup in wallet_keypool_topup (w0xlt)

Pull request description:

  `wallet_keypool_topup.py` is meant to test keypool restore for four output types, one node each. But the wallet and backup paths are only set for node1, so for nodes 2-4 the test copies node1's backup over node1's running wallet and restarts the node under test on its own, never-restored wallet. The checks still pass, so only the legacy case has actually been tested since 0dcac51049.

  This backs up and restores each node's own wallet, and asserts that the restored wallet rescans on startup so the test can't silently skip the restore again. Adding just that assertion on master makes the test fail at node2.

  Also fixes `wallet_createwallet.py` calling `w7.walletpassphrase` where it means w8 (since c5d3787367), so the `avoid_reuse wallet` was never checked.

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#35756: cmake: De-duplicate libraries where possible

e6c1483832e018ccafc04fdc4faf051d13fc09d4 guix: Turn macOS linker warnings into errors (Hennadii Stepanov)
1714370aa60ce88941ae95b06f4eb6d7dae1650a cmake: De-duplicate libraries where possible (Hennadii Stepanov)

Pull request description:

  Set the [CMP0156](https://cmake.org/cmake/help/latest/policy/CMP0156.html) and [CMP0179](https://cmake.org/cmake/help/latest/policy/CMP0179.html) policies to NEW. CMP0156 de-duplicates libraries on link lines based on linker capabilities; CMP0179 makes this de-duplication keep the first occurrence of static libraries. This silences Apple linker "ignoring duplicate libraries" warnings.

  Both policies are gated on CMP0179, which requires CMake >=3.31, to avoid the intermediate CMake 3.29/3.30 behaviour where only CMP0156 is available. This requirement is satisfied by the current Homebrew package and the Guix build environment. On older versions, the policy guard makes this a no-op.

  The Guix scripts for macOS have been updated to turn linker warnings into errors, as is [done](https://github.com/fanquake/bitcoin/commit/1714953eff0544d6085c4c1cc4270a891dd995c0) for other targets.

commit.message:
Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#35474: node: move index ownership to NodeContext

bb357fcd2fc55807905868e3c394579306ec4b44 node: move block filter index ownership to NodeContext (woltx)
66892cdd56338c4e780c05cfd8d8045f09a826bb net_processing: get block filter index via PeerManager::Options (woltx)
e5b76bbdbba852a0072b3d2b52cb41c7785c495e rpc: get index info from NodeContext indexes (woltx)
fafedc683a74b3b1fab58f8df2dfd9c1516fee15 node: move coinstatsindex ownership to NodeContext (woltx)
2d1dc8f18a2a781ac9c5e40435165d821e0ca410 node: move txospenderindex ownership to NodeContext (woltx)
530cf35c17fc07456a7837e4806be5360c939f91 node: move txindex ownership to NodeContext (woltx)

Pull request description:

  This removes the remaining process-global index ownership and stores node-owned indexes in `NodeContext` instead.

  Indexes moved:

  - `g_txindex`
  - `g_txospenderindex`
  - `g_coin_stats_index`
  - `g_filter_indexes`

  `NodeContext` now owns these index instances, while `node.indexes` remains a non-owning list used for common index startup, shutdown, and `getindexinfo` handling.

  Behavior should be unchanged, apart from the key order in `getindexinfo` output. Indexes are still created from the same startup options, started in the same init step, stopped before destruction, and destroyed while `validation_signals` is still alive so they can unregister safely.

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36924: test: Speed up interface_ipc_mining.py and fix large timeout-factor bug

Pull request description:

  The test would fail with a large enough timeout factor, because the ipc
  times out before the delayed `generate()` call: `template2` would be `None`
  and fail the assert.

  Also, the test would sleep more than timeout_factor seconds in the happy
  case in all test runs.

  Fix both issues by sleeping for a bit longer than a single fee tick.

commit.message:
Merge bitcoin-core/gui#947: Update RPC console wallet when the active wallet changes

9ee30341032cdd414d6b74c9ebe97fb8daf1b320 gui: Update RPC console wallet when the active wallet changes (Kyle 🐆)

Pull request description:

  When multiple wallets are loaded, switching the active wallet via the main window's wallet selector doesn't update the wallet used by the RPC console. Console commands keep running against the previously selected wallet, so a wallet RPC can be sent to a different wallet than the one shown as active.

  The open/create/restore/migrate paths already call `RPCConsole::setCurrentWallet()`, but the main window selector was missed. Add the call to the central `setCurrentWallet()`.

  To reproduce: load two wallets, switch the active wallet in the toolbar, then run a wallet command such as `getwalletinfo` in the console.

      |        ^~~~~
1 warning generated.
```

doc: spell out escape sequences in doxygen comments

Doxygen interprets a backslash followed by a letter as a command, so
'\n' renders as a line break and '\t' etc. are unknown commands.
